newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Prospect of auctions weigh on Belgian OLOs.
newsitem.headline: Prospect of auctions weigh on Belgian OLOs.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds recovered early weakness but still trailed Bunds on Monday, with the prospect of an exchange auction Tuesday and monthly OLO sale next week causing the 10 year yield spead to edge out slightly.
By 1655 GMT the benchmark 2006 OLO was yielding 5.98 percent, unchanged from Friday's close after opening at 6.00 percent on Monday and touching 5.97 in the late afternoon.

"There are no end-investors - just people who are playing Belgian bonds against others," one dealer said. The prospect of the OLO auctions was the main reason for the spread over Bunds widening to 17 basis points, he added.
However the prospect of an OLO coming to maturity at the same time as the auction on November 25 would bring extra liquidity to help mop up the surplus paper.

Belgian media reports linking one of the country's deputy prime ministers, Elio Di Rupo, with a possible sex scandal were also causing an air of uncertainty, though this was weighing on the Belgian franc more than the bond market, dealers said.
The franc eased slightly to the mark and stood at 20.6110/20 in late afternoon trading compared with Friday's close of 20.6075/90.
Analysts said the Belgian government as a whole did not so far appear threatened by the current wave of scandals washing across the country, even if the heads of certain individuals were to roll.
